title: Feed A Crowd: Pumpkin and Pea Laksa
subtitle: Cook Once, Serve More!
description: Serve up more with our Feed A Crowd recipes! Using more hearty ingredients like filling carbs, proteins and veggies, you can satisfy extra hungry tummies or keep something for tomorrow’s lunch. If you’re on a 2-person plan, these recipes make 4 portions; on a 4-person plan, they make 8 portions.

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Preheat the oven to 220C, fan-forced. Line a large oven tray with baking paper. Halve the unpeeled pumpkin widthwise, then cut into 8 wedges. Remove the skin from half the wedges. Pick the coriander leaves and finely chop the stems, keeping them separate. Crush or finely chop the garlic.

Roast pumpkin: Put the unpeeled pumpkin wedges on the lined tray and drizzle with 1 tbs vegetable oil. Season with salt and pepper and turn to coat. Roast, turning the wedges halfway, for 20 mins or until tender. Meanwhile, bring a large saucepan of water to the boil for the noodles.

Cook laksa: Heat 1 tbs vegetable oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Cook the peeled pumpkin wedges, coriander stems, garlic and curry powder, stirring, for 1 min or until fragrant. Add the coconut milk, 2 tbs soy sauce, 1 tbs white vinegar and 1L (4 cups) water, stir to combine and bring to the boil (see Feed A Crowd).

Cook noodles: Reduce the heat to medium and cook the laksa, stirring occasionally, for 12 mins or until the pumpkin is tender. Mash the pumpkin in the laksa with a spoon. Add the peas and cook for a further 3 mins or until just tender. Taste, then season with salt and pepper. Remove the pan from the heat. Meanwhile, cook the noodles in the pan of boiling water for 9 mins or until tender. Drain.

Serve up: Bring a small saucepan of water to the boil for the eggs. Cook 2 eggs in the pan of boiling water for 6 mins for soft-boiled or 8 mins for hard-boiled. Drain, then cool in cold water. Peel and halve the eggs. Divide the noodles among bowls and spoon over the laksa. Top with the roast pumpkin wedges, egg, coriander leaves and peanuts. Enjoy!
Feed A Crowd: Depending on your palate, you may want to add a pinch of sugar to the laksa to help balance out the acidity of the vinegar.
